bug_description.normalized: A 13-byte wasm witness `00 61 73 6d 01 00 00 00 09 03 01 00 91` makes `ReadSections` parse an elem section with declared size 3, so `read_end_` ends exactly after payload bytes `01 00 91`. `ReadElemSection` then parses one active element segment whose init expression contains only `Opcode::F32Sqrt` and no terminating `END`. `ReadInitExpr` still returns `Ok`, `BinaryReaderObjdump` records one init instruction without ever assigning `current_init_expr_.type`, and `InitExprToConstOffset` later switches on that uninitialized type.

source.description: First project parser read on the vulnerable path: it materializes the attacker-controlled section code that dispatches into the element-section parser.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is the 13-byte blob `00 61 73 6d 01 00 00 00 09 03 01 00 91`. After the wasm magic/version, the next two bytes are the element-section header `09 03`. This statement consumes `0x09` as `section_code = BinarySection::Elem`; the following trace step consumes `0x03` as the declared section size.
source.note: Because the section code is `Elem`, `ReadSections` stays on the element-section dispatch path and the next header step computes the 3-byte section boundary later reused by `ReadInitExpr`.

root_cause.description: The init-expression reader delegates to `ReadInstructions` with the section-end bound `read_end_` but discards the final opcode, so falling out at section end is treated as successful completion even when no `END` opcode was seen.
root_cause.note: For this witness, `ReadSections` derived `read_end_ = 0x0d` from the section-size byte `0x03`. After the lone `0x91` opcode is consumed, `ReadInstructions` exits its `while (state_.offset < end_offset)` loop at that boundary and returns `Ok` from line 1829 without hitting `case Opcode::End`. The staged fix records `final_opcode` and rejects any init expression whose last opcode was not `End`.

sink.description: MSAN crash site where the objdump helper reads the uninitialized init-expression type.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `src/binary-reader-objdump.cc:1811:5` in `InitExprToConstOffset`, with callers `BinaryReaderObjdump::EndInitExpr -> BinaryReaderObjdump::EndElemSegmentInitExpr -> ReadElemSection`.

parser_admitted.description: After `ReadSections` dispatches `section_code = BinarySection::Elem`, control enters `ReadElemSection`, so the trace is inside the project element-section parser rather than the libFuzzer boundary.

tainted_value_origin.description: The direct attacker-controlled opcode byte that populates the malformed init expression.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: In the exact witness, byte `0x91` is the only remaining byte in the 3-byte element section after the flags field. `src/opcode.def` maps `0x91` to `Opcode::F32Sqrt`.
tainted_value_origin.note: This is the byte that becomes the sole recorded init-expression instruction and later makes `expr.insts.size() == 1` at the sink.

coarse_trace.summary: For the harness's line-30 Headers call, `ReadBinaryObjdump` takes its default branch and stack-allocates the `BinaryReaderObjdump` object whose `current_init_expr_.type` remains indeterminate.
The section reader consumes header bytes `09 03`, identifies an element section, and sets `read_end_` to the end of that 3-byte payload.
The element-section parser reads one segment with `flags = 0`, so it enters the active-segment init-expression path.
Beginning the element init expression clears `current_init_expr_.insts` but leaves `current_init_expr_.type` untouched.
The truncated init expression contributes a sole `f32.sqrt` opcode.
The delegate records one `InitInst` for that opcode without assigning an init-expression type.
Section-end is accepted as successful init-expression completion because `ReadInstructions(..., read_end_, NULL)` falls out at `read_end_` without an `END`.
`CHECK_RESULT(ReadInitExpr(i))` sees `Ok`, so the element parser continues to the end-init callback.
The malformed active element init expression is finalized and passed to the offset-conversion helper.
The offset helper sees a one-instruction init expression and switches on the uninitialized `expr.type`, triggering MSAN.

fine_trace.note: In the default `BinaryReaderObjdump` branch used by the harness's line-30 Headers call, wabt stack-allocates `reader` (`reader8` in the MSAN origin) and aliases the fuzz buffer into it. `InitExpr` has no field initializer, and the constructor initializer list never writes `current_init_expr_`, so `current_init_expr_.type` starts as indeterminate stack data.
After the 8-byte wasm magic/version, this reads witness byte `0x09` as `section_code = BinarySection::Elem`, identifying the next section as an element section.
Consumes the next header byte `0x03` as `section_size = 3`, meaning the entire element-section payload is exactly the following three bytes `01 00 91`.

At this point `state_.offset` is 10, so `read_end_` becomes `13` (`0x0d`), the end of the 13-byte witness. This boundary is the `end_offset` later passed into `ReadInitExpr`/`ReadInstructions` for the whole element section.
Because `section_code` selected `BinarySection::Elem`, control enters `ReadElemSection` and reads the first payload byte `0x01` as `num_elem_segments = 1`, so exactly one segment iteration executes.
In the sole segment iteration, the next payload byte `0x00` is decoded as `flags = 0`.
With `flags = 0`, the segment is active, so control enters the init-expression path and calls `BeginElemSegmentInitExpr`/`ReadInitExpr` instead of taking the passive-segment path.
The delegate marks that it is reading an element init expression and `BeginInitExpr()` clears only `current_init_expr_.insts`. The indeterminate `current_init_expr_.type` from step 1 is preserved.

`ReadInitExpr(i)` starts `ReadInstructions` with `end_offset = read_end_`. The only remaining section byte, `0x91`, is read as `Opcode::F32Sqrt`, leaving `state_.offset == read_end_ == 0x0d` and no bytes available for an `END` opcode or the later `elem count` LEB.

fine_trace.code: if (ReadingInitExpr() && opcode != Opcode::End) { InitInst i; i.opcode = current_opcode; current_init_expr_.insts.push_back(i); }
fine_trace.note: Because the delegate is inside an init expression and the opcode is not `END`, it appends one `InitInst` for `f32.sqrt`. No later type-setting callback runs for this unary opcode, so `current_init_expr_.insts.size()` becomes 1 while `current_init_expr_.type` remains uninitialized.

After step 9 consumes the last byte in the 3-byte section, `ReadInstructions` exits its `while (state_.offset < end_offset)` loop at `read_end_` and returns `Result::Ok` from line 1829 without hitting `case Opcode::End`. Because `ReadInitExpr` passed `NULL` for `final_opcode`, it performs no end-marker check and accepts plain section end as a valid init-expression terminator.

depends_on.via: state_.offset == read_end_ after the lone opcode

fine_trace.note: The caller observes `ReadInitExpr(i)` as `Ok`, so control stays on the normal element-segment path and immediately proceeds to `CALLBACK(EndElemSegmentInitExpr, i);` at line 2677 instead of rejecting the malformed init expression.
The active element-segment epilogue now treats the partial init expression as finished and forwards `current_init_expr_` to `InitExprToConstOffset` to derive `elem_offset_`.

Sink. The malformed init expression still has exactly one recorded instruction, so this helper enters the switch and reads `expr.type`. That field originated as uninitialized stack data in step 1, step 8 only preserved it, and no callback assigned it before this switch, so MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at line 1811.

allocation_context.note: MemorySanitizer reports that the uninitialized value was created by stack allocation of `reader8` in `ReadBinaryObjdump`; the concrete `BinaryReaderObjdump reader(data, size, options, state);` statement is line 2383.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_51568 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, fed the staged `poc` to `/out/wasm_objdump_fuzzer`, printed `000000d: error: unable to read u32 leb128: elem count`, and then reproduced `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `InitExprToConstOffset`; the saved stack returns to `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` at `wasm_objdump_fuzzer.cc:30`, the harness's Headers-mode call into `ReadBinaryObjdump`.

format.name: 13-byte malformed WebAssembly binary with a truncated active element-segment init expression
format.contract: Exactly the staged 13-byte wasm blob with SHA-256 `543e502d248494cdd98e67b4f339cacb7b0eecd88b52a939d8f5d384a0fd58bf` and bytes `00 61 73 6d 01 00 00 00 09 03 01 00 91`. Static parsing of that witness yields a valid wasm magic/version followed by an elem section header `09 03`. `ReadSections` consumes `0x09` as `BinarySection::Elem`, consumes `0x03` as `section_size = 3`, and sets `read_end_ = 0x0d`, so the section payload is exactly `01 00 91`: `num_elem_segments = 1`, `flags = 0` (active segment), and a single init-expression opcode byte `0x91`, which `src/opcode.def` maps to `Opcode::F32Sqrt`. No bytes remain for a terminating `Opcode::End` or for the mandatory following `elem count` LEB. In the saved crash trace, `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` returns to `wasm_objdump_fuzzer.cc:30`, which is the harness's Headers-mode call into `ReadBinaryObjdump`; that default `BinaryReaderObjdump` path lets `ReadInitExpr(i)` fall out at `read_end_` as success, records one `f32.sqrt` init instruction without initializing `current_init_expr_.type`, and then switches on that uninitialized field in `InitExprToConstOffset`. The staged artifacts justify this exact truncated element-section witness and do not independently prove a broader input class.
